text:
maya: quick Q — we're finalizing the KMS design for Redwood Private (VPC). need buy-in on: control-plane CMK vs data-plane CMKs, audit hooks, and rotation playbooks. any red flags?

sam: i'm thinking: control-plane CMK in customer's acct (BYOK) for config blobs; data-plane DEKs encrypted under a dedicated CMK per-tenant or per-region? pros/cons?

jordan: per-tenant CMK is safest for isolation but explosion of keys + limits. per-region + tenant-namespace via encryption context is middle ground. also grants help for short-lived worker access instead of IAM perms.

lee: agree on grants. one operational note: CloudTrail only surfaces KMS events at API-level — you need to capture "Encrypt","Decrypt","GenerateDataKey" events and inspect encryptionContext in logs for multitenancy auditing.

maya: concrete ask: example KMS key policy + minimal IAM role for control plane to call GenerateDataKey, and a sample rotation procedure for when customer rotates their CMK.

sam: posting sample policy and a quick CLI snippet — use grants for runtime access and avoid putting production workers in key policy where possible.

infra-bot: policy snippet (example):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::CUSTOMER_ACC:role/redwood-controlplane"},
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey*","kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*"] ,
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:ViaService": "ec2.amazonaws.com"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

jordan: small tweak — avoid wildcards in Action for production. include specific actions. Also add `kms:EncryptionContext:CustomerID` condition to limit misuse.

sam: rotation flow we use in other teams: 1) provision new CMK, 2) update alias to point to new key only after new DEKs re-encrypted or after dual-write window, 3) run async rewrap job for persisted blobs, 4) shorten DEK cache TTL during transition, 5) monitor CloudTrail errors and metrics.

maya: how do we handle incoming requests during alias swap if some workers still have old DEKs in cache? risk of Decrypt failing.

lee: plan for that: dual-decrypt support — try decrypt with current CMK alias then fallback to previous key ARN, and add metrics when fallback occurs. limit fallback window to TTL. set DEK cache TTL to something like 5m during rollout.

oncall-bot: note — escalate if >1% decrypt errors across a 5m window after alias swap. runbook: rotate-dek, revoke-grants, fallback-route, page oncall.

maya: two more things: 1) envelope encryption context design — include tenant_id, model_id, and intent hash; 2) incident steps for suspected key compromise.

jordan: sample encryption context keys: `{"tenant_id":"T-123","resource":"controlplane-config","purpose":"dataplane-dek"}`. ensures logs show mapping and prevents accidental cross-tenant decrypt if context enforced.

sam: incident hdl: 1) disable key (schedule/disable via KMS API) 2) create new CMK + grants 3) force rewrap of stored DEKs 4) revoke existing data-plane sessions and rotate session tokens 5) audit CloudTrail for suspicious Decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls 6) notify customer + compliance.

maya: can we get a short playbook snippet for the runbook doc? i'll paste this into the private runbook repo once we agree.

lee: i'll draft runbook: commands to list grants, revoke, disable CMK, rewrap job example (aws kms re-encrypt), and monitoring queries for CloudWatch/Elasticsearch.

infra-bot: helpful CLI bits:
```
# re-encrypt an object (example)
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc.dat --source-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/old --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/new --destination-encryption-context '{"tenant_id":"T-123"}'

# list grants
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/old

# disable key
aws kms disable-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/old
```

maya: perfect. last Q: any opinion on using CMK rotation (automatic KMS rotation) vs manual new key+alias swap for compliance customers?

jordan: auto-rotation is OK for convenience but you lose ability to rewrap on a controlled schedule and to maintain old-key fallback semantics. for enterprise compliance we usually prefer manual new-key + alias swap with documented rewrap window.

sam: +1. note that if customer mandates HSM-backed CMKs (CloudHSM), test performance for high-throughput data-plane decrypts — might need a caching layer for DEKs.

maya: thanks all — i'll incorporate into the runbook and circle back with a PR. tagging @sam @lee for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
